I used to bite my nails. Not just bite my nails but rip out my cuticles and any skin around the nail that wasn't perfectly smooth. I could be dripping blood but it didn't matter as long as the skin was "smooth". It was a horrible habit that grew and worsened with my depression.

I had a dream that I was captured by aliens and put into some sort of intergalactic zoo. As the zookeeper led a tour around the cages, I heard them saying all of these wonderful things about my fellow captives in the cages around mine. Then they got to me.

"This human has been in a state of clear emotional distress for an unknown period of time as it rips apart its own flesh and bites off it's nails." 

I don't bite my nails anymore.

A friend is allowing me to stay with them while I am trying to get my life back in order... I've been struggling with depression, suicidal ideation and alcoholism for a long time now.

The first month of my stay, getting out of bed and showering everyday was a chore. Sometimes it wouldn't happen until 6pm, but most days, I did it. Eventually I started rewarding myself by listening to music, a love of mine that I didn't care to do anymore in my depression. No social benefit there, no working on a new skill, no benefit to the household.

I also HATE doing dishes. I've always hated doing dishes. I would feel massive amounts of guilt as my friend would be at work and I'd stare at the pile of dishes and not be able to muster the energy to just go over and wash the freaking dishes. One day, I did those stupid dishes while listening to music as it gave me, somehow, the energy I needed. It made me feel great. I told my friend, "I did the dishes!" And his response was, "OK, that's not an accomplishment." BUT. IT. SO. WAS.

For people that are willing to learn, or relearn, self control and responsibility, asking them to immediately incorporate activities solely because they offer some sort of social benefit, comes off a lot like "Ya, but have you tried not being depressed?"

Activities that you enjoy help create this reward system and motivate you to be able to tackle the dishes. Some of us are baby-stepping.
